title: Noetherian descent of a reductive pair with a framed torus weight decomposition
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $G/S$ a reductive group, with the meaning of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Let $M$ be a finite-rank free abelian group and $T=D_A(M)\hookrightarrow G$ a closed subgroup [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group, def-weil-closed-immersion] maximal among tori on every geometric fibre. Put $\mathfrak g=\ker(G(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G(A))$ with its tangent $A$-module structure, and let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g\otimes_A A[M]$ be the conjugation coaction. Let $\Psi\subset M\setminus\{0\}$ be finite and choose vectors $X_b\in\mathfrak g$ for $b\in\Psi$ such that $\rho(X_b)=X_b\otimes e^b$ and the natural map
$$\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{b\in\Psi}A X_b\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak g$$
is an isomorphism, with each $A X_b$ free of rank one on the indicated generator.

There exist a subring $A_0\subseteq A$ generated by finitely many elements over $\mathbf Z$, a reductive group $G_0/\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, a closed split torus $T_0=D_{A_0}(M)\hookrightarrow G_0$ maximal on every geometric fibre, vectors $X_{b,0}\in\operatorname{Lie}(G_0)$, and an $A$-group-scheme isomorphism $(G_0)_A\simeq G$. Its restriction to $(T_0)_A=T$ is the given inclusion, and its differential sends $1\otimes X_{b,0}$ to $X_b$. Write $\rho_0$ for conjugation by $T_0$. One has $\rho_0(X_{b,0})=X_{b,0}\otimes e^b$ and
$$\operatorname{Lie}(G_0)=\operatorname{Lie}(T_0)\oplus\bigoplus_{b\in\Psi}A_0 X_{b,0},$$
with every indicated root summand free on its displayed generator. The natural tangent comparison $A\otimes_{A_0}\operatorname{Lie}(G_0)\simeq\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ respects these decompositions and the full torus coactions. The ring $A_0$ is nonzero and Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. On every geometric fibre of $G_0$ the nonzero torus weights are exactly $\Psi$; its semisimple rank is $\dim_{\mathbf Q}\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}(\Psi)$. Here semisimple rank means the dimension of a maximal torus in the quotient of the fibre group by its largest smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial. In particular, for $\Psi=\{a,-a\}$, $a\ne0$, every geometric fibre has semisimple rank one. The case $\Psi=\varnothing$ is allowed. No reducedness, connectedness, characteristic or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Corollary 3.1.11 and proof, printed pp.88-89 (descent of reductivity along ring limits); introduction to Section 4, pp.107-108 (full torus weight subbundles and base change); Section 1.3, pp.25-29 (root datum and semisimple rank). Agent extraction with a finite list of tangent basis vectors and their coaction identities included in the finite-presentation data. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states descent of this entire framed reductive structure.

proof.text: Choose an integral basis of $M$ of size $r$. By [lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras], the finitely generated integer subrings $A_i\subseteq A$ form a small nonempty directed system with colimit $A$. Each is nonzero because it has the same unit as $A$. Every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is principal, so $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes every $A_i$ Noetherian. The spectra $S_i$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], have affine transitions, and have scheme limit $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. We may replace this system by any tail after choosing a stage.

source.place: Finite coefficient subrings; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Limits Tag 01YW

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$. The affine smoothness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] supplies a finite presentation $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$. Choose one $A_i$ containing all coefficients of the $f_j$ and use the same quotient to define $C_i$. Its extension to $A$ is the specified presentation of $C$. Keep $T_i=D_{A_i}(M)$ fixed, with algebra $L_i=A_i[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ and its usual Hopf operations; this is finitely presented using variables $z_j,w_j$ and relations $z_jw_j-1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], tensor products of these algebras represent all group products and base changes. They, including the triple products, are finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-product-finitely-presented-algebras].

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, proof (1); Tags 00F4, 05G5; affine smoothness Tags 01V6, 02H6

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras] to the coordinate maps of multiplication, identity, inverse on $G$, and of the given inclusion $T\to G$. At one upper bound they are maps between the fixed stage algebras. Apply clause (3) to the following finite list of pairs: the associativity composites, the left and right unit composites, the left and right inverse composites, and the multiplication, identity and inverse compatibilities of $T_i\to G_i$. All pairs agree after extension to $A$, so at a common later stage they agree. Thus $G_i$ is a group scheme and $j_i:T_i\to G_i$ a homomorphism. The presentation comparison $G_{i,A}\simeq G$ preserves the operations and carries $j_{i,A}$ to the given inclusion. This is descent of actual maps and equations, without a faithful-flatness assumption on $A_i\to A$.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, (2) and (3), finite list of group and homomorphism diagrams

proof.text: Both $S_i,G_i,T_i$ are affine and hence qcqs. The structure map of $G_i$ is locally of finite presentation from its explicit algebra presentation. The morphism $j_i$ is locally of finite type: the Laurent generators of $L_i$ over $A_i$ also generate it over $C_i$ via $j_i^*$. Its limit is the given closed immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] makes $j_i$ closed at a later stage. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-smooth-qcqs] to $G_i\to S_i$ to make it smooth. Closedness persists on the tail because tensoring a surjective coordinate map remains surjective. The same cited smooth-descent statement supplies smoothness on the entire tail. Now [lem-sfb-reductivity-eventual-ring-colimit] applies to this smooth affine finitely presented group with reductive limit $G$. Enlarge once more to make every remaining $G_i$ reductive on all of $S_i$.

source.place: Tags 01ZP and 0C0C, lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation and lemma-descend-smooth; Conrad Corollary 3.1.11, pp.88-89

proof.text: Fix this reductive stage $i$. Let $E\subset S_i$ be the locus where $T_i$ is a geometric maximal torus. The maximality clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-fibre-openness] says $E$ is open. The limit image lies in $E$: at a point of $S$, compare algebraic closures of its residue field and of the contracted residue field in a common algebraically closed extension; maximality is preserved and reflected by [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension]. Since $A_i$ is Noetherian, the ideal generated by all $f$ with $D(f)\subset E$ has finitely many generators, hence $E$ is a finite union of principal opens. Principal opens and their intersections are affine and qcqs, so they are retrocompact; therefore $E$ is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] to obtain a later stage whose whole image is in $E$. Field-extension invariance again proves that its torus is maximal on every geometric fibre. Retain its tail; the torus is still exactly $D_{A_j}(M)$.

source.place: Tag 05F4, lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible; Conrad Proposition 3.1.9, maximality argument, pp.85-86

proof.text: At this stage put $V_i=\operatorname{Lie}(G_i)$ and $W_i=\operatorname{Lie}(T_i)$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] to the conjugation actions and, for $T_i$, its trivial self-conjugation. The base ring is nonzero Noetherian, and both groups are smooth affine of finite type (for $T_i$, lift each Laurent unit $u$ and its inverse $v$ across a square-zero ideal $I$; if $uv=1+t$, $t\in I$, then $v(1-t)$ is its inverse, which proves formal smoothness for its finite presentation). It gives finite projectivity, the full torus coactions, and tangent comparisons for every later $A_j$ and for $A$. In the chosen basis of $M$, the torus tangent module is $A_i^r$: a tangent point sends $z_k$ to $1+\epsilon a_k$, and $w_k$ to $1-\epsilon a_k$. The differential $d j_i:W_i\to V_i$ is natural under all these comparisons: it is postcomposition of the same dual-number points with $j_i$, which commutes with scalar extension. The comparison for $G_{i,A}\simeq G$ is obtained in exactly this way.

source.place: Background on Lie functors, p.2; Section 4 introduction, p.107; explicit Laurent dual-number coordinates

proof.text: Let $F_i=W_i\oplus A_i^{\Psi}$ and define $F_j$ by extension. All $F_i,V_i$ are finitely presented: if $V_i$ is the image of an idempotent $e$ on $A_i^n$, then $V_i$ is the cokernel of $1-e:A_i^n\to A_i^n$; $F_i$ is finite free by step 6. The given decomposition over $A$ is a specified linear isomorphism $f_A:F_A\to V_A$, whose torus component is $d j_A$ and whose $b$-th coordinate is $X_b$. By the map clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine], descend $f_A$ and its inverse to maps $f_j:F_j\to V_j$, $h_j:V_j\to F_j$. By its equality clause, enlarge so that $h_jf_j=1$, $f_jh_j=1$, and $f_j|_{W_j}=d j_j$. Define $X_{b,j}=f_j(e_b)$. These vectors pull back to the specified $X_b$, and $f_j$ is already an isomorphism with exactly the required torus component. All these equalities remain valid under later extension.

source.place: Tag 05N7, lemma-colimit-category-fp-modules, (2),(3), applied to maps, inverse identities and the torus-component equality

proof.text: For every $b\in\Psi$, form $q_b=\rho_j(X_{b,j})-X_{b,j}\otimes e^b$ in $V_j\otimes_{A_j} A_j[M]$. There is a canonical coefficient expansion $V_j\otimes A_j[M]=\bigoplus_{m\in M}V_j$: the forward map sends $v\otimes\sum a_me^m$ to $(a_mv)_m$, and its inverse sends a finite family to $\sum v_m\otimes e^m$. Thus each $q_b$ has finitely many coefficients. By the tangent-coaction comparison of step 6, every coefficient becomes zero over $A$, since $X_b$ has weight $b$. Regard each such coefficient as a map $A_j\to V_j$, $1\mapsto v_m$. The equality clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine], comparing this map with zero, kills it at some later stage. There are finitely many $b$ and finitely many coefficients for each, so take one upper bound. At that stage, now called $0$, all identities $\rho_0(X_{b,0})=X_{b,0}\otimes e^b$ hold. The inverse identities of step 7 still hold.

source.place: Tag 05N7, lemma-colimit-category-fp-modules, (3), coefficientwise on the finite Laurent supports; Conrad p.107 for full coaction comparison

proof.text: The isomorphism $f_0$ now identifies $V_0$ with $W_0\oplus\bigoplus_{b\in\Psi}A_0e_b$. Its restriction to $W_0$ is the actual differential of the torus inclusion, so this differential is injective and each $A_0X_{b,0}$ is free on its displayed generator. Conjugation fixes $\operatorname{Lie}(T_0)$ because $T_0$ is commutative: over every algebra, $tut^{-1}=u$ for $u\in T_0(R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$. Therefore the full coaction on this summand is $w\mapsto w\otimes1$. Together with step 8, $f_0$ is an isomorphism of full torus comodules. Extend its two inverse maps to $A$ and compose with the tangent comparison of step 6. On $W_A$ the result is the given inclusion; on $e_b$ it is $X_b$. Hence it is precisely the given decomposition and respects the complete conjugation coactions, rather than only their character differentials.

source.place: Section 4 introductory full-torus grading, p.107; explicit identification from the descended inverse maps

proof.text: For any geometric fibre $F$ of $A_0$, the same tangent comparison and the scalar extension of $f_0,h_0$ give $\operatorname{Lie}(G_F)=\operatorname{Lie}(T_F)\oplus\bigoplus_{b\in\Psi}F X_{b,F}$. Every displayed generator remains nonzero because these maps are inverse after tensoring. Distinct $b\in M$ give distinct monomials even in positive characteristic. Comparing coefficients in the free basis $(e^m)_{m\in M}$ shows that the nonzero full-torus weights are exactly $\Psi$. This also covers $\Psi=\varnothing$: the entire tangent module then has weight zero.

source.place: Section 4 introduction, p.107; coefficient comparison in the specified free decomposition

proof.text: It remains to compute the fibre semisimple rank; fix such an algebraically closed $F$ and put $H=G_F$. By [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel], applied over the Noetherian field $F$, $Z(H)=D_F(M/\mathbf Z\Psi)$. Let $L=M\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}(\Psi)\subset M\otimes\mathbf Q$ and $N=M/L$. This $N$ is finitely generated and torsion-free (if $nv\in L$, then $v\in L$), so [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] gives an integral basis. By [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality], $K=D_F(N)$ is a closed subtorus of $Z(H)$. Every subtorus $C\subseteq Z(H)$ corresponds to a surjection $M/\mathbf Z\Psi\to X^*(C)$; its free target kills the torsion subgroup $L/\mathbf Z\Psi$, so this factors through $N$. The same duality says $C\subseteq K$. Thus $K$ is the largest central torus. By [lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient], it is the radical $R(H)$, and the quotient $H/K$ is the represented semisimple quotient whose maximal-torus dimension defines the semisimple rank of $H$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.6, p.101; Section 1.3, pp.25-29; lattice computation of the largest central torus

proof.text: Write $d=\dim_{\mathbf Q}\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}(\Psi)$. The rational quotient $(M/L)\otimes\mathbf Q=(M\otimes\mathbf Q)/\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}(\Psi)$ has dimension $r-d$, so $K\simeq\mathbf G_m^{r-d}$. [lem-ag-lie-identity-tangent-equiv] identifies Lie and tangent spaces at the identity. A split torus of rank $s$ has tangent dimension $s$: the $s$ coordinates are $1+\epsilon a_j$. It is smooth by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus], and [lem-sfb-group-tangent-dimension-smoothness] therefore gives its Krull dimension $s$. Hence $\dim T_F=r$ and $\dim K=r-d$. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-semisimple-rank-formula] to the central radical $K$. It contains every smooth connected normal subgroup $P$ whose successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial: that derived series is a chain of closed subgroups, each normal in its predecessor with commutative quotient (Milne, Proposition 6.30), so $P$ is solvable in the sense of [lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient] and $P\subseteq R(H)=K$ by step 11; $K$ itself is commutative. It gives semisimple rank $r-(r-d)=d$. For $\Psi=\{a,-a\}$, $a\ne0$ in the free lattice, $d=1$; for the empty set $d=0$. Taking the final stage as $A_0,G_0,T_0$ proves all assertions; $A_0$ is a nonzero Noetherian finitely generated integer subring by step 1.

source.place: Section 1.3, pp.25-29; Milne Algebraic Groups, Proposition 17.20 and Corollaries 17.61-17.62, pp.357-358,372-373; Milne Algebraic Groups, Proposition 6.30 (solvable iff the derived series terminates)
